name: Front split (passive hold)

technique.setup: Kneel in a low lunge on a mat with a folded towel under the back knee and a stack of books or yoga blocks either side of the front foot. Slide the front heel forward and the back knee back only as far as is comfortable, hands on the books. To measure progress, sit at your lowest comfortable point and measure the gap in cm from the floor to the front of your pelvis, left and right side forward separately.
cues: Keep the hips square to the front
Point the back knee straight down into the floor
Breathe out and let the hips sink slowly
No pain, only a stretch sensation: back off if it bites
mistakes: Twisting the back hip open to get lower
Bouncing to force depth
Dropping all your weight onto the floor instead of the hands
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the hip, groin or knee
Tingling or numbness down the back of the front leg
Pinching at the front of the hip

name: Front split PNF (contract-relax)

technique.setup: Set up exactly as for the passive front split, on books or blocks, and settle at a comfortable depth for 20 s. Then press the front heel down into the floor at about 30% effort for 5 s, relax for 3 s and sink a little lower; repeat 2-3 times. Measure floor distance the same way as the passive hold.
cues: Press the front heel down gently, about 30% effort
Breathe out as you relax and sink
Keep the hips square and the hands on the books
No pain, only a stretch sensation
mistakes: Contracting at full effort
Sinking further than the new comfortable depth
Doing it before jumps or other explosive work
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the hip, groin or knee
Tingling or numbness down the back of the leg
A cramp in the hamstring that does not settle

Lift from the hip, not by leaning back
Hold 2 s at the top, lower in 2 s
Work near the end of your range, never into pain

Rocking the torso back to cheat the heel up
